measurementPlan.failureContext: RE-ISSUED in rev 2 as failurePathRule below. It keeps rev 1's three triggering cases and its 'no substituted number' prohibition, but replaces the 'log-plan record' requirement with two carriers that really exist in this project: source-comment documentation, and the absence of the affected parameter's result.

failurePathRule.noNewNumbers: the rule introduces no new voltage, current, threshold, limit or tolerance; every judgement uses values this item itself wrote into, or read back from, its own calls

cases.requiredBehaviour: no value may be published for <base>_Rise / <base>_Fall at that site - including any initialised or defaulted number held by the result array - and Hys must not be computed from a segment without a capture. Not publishing the value IS the record.
cases.capabilityStatus: UNKNOWN whether the primitive reports 'no trigger' at all (functions-registry.md:43 registers only 'result = the voltage at the trigger point' and no failure signal). This contract therefore names no detection primitive, states the obligation only, and carries the gap as OI-T5-07. Until it closes, a no-capture segment must be treated as an unclosed failure path, NOT as a conformant one - which is also why this is not written up as a code defect (consistent with the review's classification of RR-02 as an INFERENCE).

cases.condition: the captured value equals one of the two endpoints the segment itself declared (the trigger fired on the sweep boundary, not at an interior threshold)
cases.requiredBehaviour: handled as the no-trigger case for publication purposes, and the endpoint that was hit is named in that site's failure record
cases.capabilityStatus: self-contained - the comparison uses only the segment's own start/stop values, so no new threshold is needed

cases.requiredBehaviour: Hys is a computed quantity, not a substitute for a missing capture, so it is published as computed: never clamped, never sign-corrected, never averaged across sites. The site must additionally be flagged as a failure-path case. Whether a negative Hys fails the item is a spec-side question (no tolerance is published - RT-4) and is not decided here.

failurePathRule.recordCarrier: The failure context (phase id, segment, reason, trigger mode, capture level, the actual start/stop/step/interval used, and which pending item was in force) is recorded as source-comment documentation in the item's own region - the same status section 6.2 gives the raw-context rows. It is NOT claimed to be a station-log record, because no station-log mechanism for free-form context exists inside the signed boundary (OI-T5-06). The station-log consequence that is available and required is the absence of the affected parameter's result.

powerDownPlan.type: normal de-energisation (no floating-source pair and no high-current loop is used by this item, so R-POFF's floating and high-current branches do not apply - rules-registry.md :33)

steps.action: Zero the scan source: VAC1 FV=0 while holding its range and leaving its relay ON.
Zero the supply: VBAT FV=0 while holding its range and leaving its relay ON (K13 still closed, so the 4.7 uF stabiliser discharges through the rail's bleed).
Zero the observation capture source: FI/FV=0 with range ACM200_10V / ACM200_10UA, relay still ON.
Release all three channels with the unified RELAY_OFF ranges (ACM200_10V/10MA, FXVIe_PLUS_10V/10MA).
Release the functional closures K13 then K65 (cap gate opening is the sanctioned rail discharge), leaving every keep-open relay un-actuated.

ruleBasis: R-POFF normal three-step (zero while holding range -> delay_ms(1) -> RELAY_OFF with unified ranges) - rules-registry.md :33
every energised rail needs a discharge plan (cap gate opened + bleed) - setup-contract.json:3943, :8177
abnormal exit runs the same sequence - setup-contract.json:8179
actualNodeVoltages: after step 4: all three driven nodes are at 0 V intent, VBAT_F is a collapsing rail with K13 still closed
after step 6: no node of this item is driven; VBAT_F/VBAT_S/VAC1_F/VAC1_S/observation node are floating with all caps released
differentialChecks: no differential pair is energised during the power-down
the only differential check that applies is the BST/SW constraint, which is NOT PROVEN for both power-down phases (see bst-sw-phase-check.md; closing evidence OI-T5-02)
